notes.title: Stability Update
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone! It's been a while since our last update. We've been working hard to fix some underlying code design issues on our end and I'm happy to say that we've made large strides. Most of these strides will be invisible to players (which is a good thing), but there are some QOL improvements we think people will enjoy as well.[/p][p][/p][p]To explain the large delay, over time, we had accumulated a large amount of code debt up until our last update and the rent came due, resulting in large amounts of code cleanup being needed to ensure that development remained consistent and stable. Code debt is a result of poor coding design decisions that, while they may work, make the code more difficult to maintain than necessary. A few of these poor decisions aren't usually a big deal, but lots of them over lifetime of a project can add up and make fixing bugs or adding features a huge chore, and making us less confident about our changes. The last thing we wanted was to push updates to you which broke things that worked, or claim we fixed things that we didn't, and this was rapidly becoming more and more likely. We've spent the last 7 months paying back our dues, and the result is a game that should be much easier to debug and improve over time.[/p][p][/p][h2]Major Improvements:[/h2][p]Lengthy explanation aside, I did mention that there are some other improvements. [b]PVP matches should remain stable[/b], and we believe starting and finishing a match should be relatively painless, perhaps less so than before. As we stated, many of the improvements we've made should not be readily apparent to players, but will very much ease development.[/p][h3][/h3][p]Added to this list, [b]we have also given you the ability to, finally, see what your opponent's cards are targeting[/b]! This can be done by hovering your mouse over a card that is in the pending position (the top left, or the top right, near the corresponding player's title bar). When doing this, the lane or the character that card will apply to will be highlighted red. You should no longer need to guess who or what a played card will affect before it happens.[/p][p][/p][p][b]We've also enhanced card inspecting.[/b] This happens when right clicking on a card, which causes the card you clicked to center and enlarge on the screen in clear view, allowing you to easily read its description and stats, or just admire the art! Previously, you could not do this for pending cards, but [b]now you should be able to do it for nearly every front-facing card, or character, you encounter in the game.[/b] We are aware that leader characters who have a flipped state cannot have their flipped side inspected unless they are currently flipped, and we'll also be fixing that in the future.[/p][p][/p][h2]Remaining Issues:[/h2][p][b]You will still encounter issues after a match finishes, or if you attempt to start another match after just having left one.[/b] This will be most noticeable when finishing a match and attempting to return to the main menu, as you may see our crash screen and be forced to close the game. If you manage to make it to the main menu after participating in a match, you may soon discover problems afterward with your next game, or even joining a lobby. [b]We recommend restarting the game completely after a match[/b] to prevent from having to encounter one of these frustrating crashes. This can be done by simply clicking the Exit Game button at the main menu. These types of critical issues will be our top priority for the next update. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Miss-clicking characters or lanes is still an issue. [/b]As before, this is due to how cursor collision is being managed. Because of how closely the shape of the collision area matches each character, you may accidentally click a lane instead of a character, the lane behind them, or even another character behind them. We understand how annoying this is, and it's also high on our list of things that need to be fixed.[/p][p][/p][h2]Final Words[/h2][p]That's it for the big stuff. As always, we really appreciate your support and we hope those of you trying this update out will enjoy the small improvements we have made, but the vast majority of this update's work is behind the scenes. We hope updates will become [b]much[/b] more frequent from now on, so please keep a lookout for future updates! [url="https://discord.gg/xgdj5jgYTh"]Please check out our Discord server[/url] to chat and give us feedback! You may also navigate to Steam's own Discussions forum in the Skirmish Community Hub on the Steam app. We'd love to hear from you![/p][p][/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/xgdj5jgYTh" style="button"]Click here to check out our Discord server[/url][/p][p][/p][h2]Full Change Log:[/h2][list][*][p]Card target visibility added by placing your cursor over a pending card.[/p][/*][*][p]Pending cards can now be focused.[/p][/*][*][p]Camera now zooms in and out smoothly, rather than stepping.[/p][/*][*][p]Music transitions properly now.[/p][/*][*][p]Better discard pile stability.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where characters would become unresponsive to declaring skirmishes or redeploying.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where cards that are being inspected will remain stuck there until certain events placed them back where they belong.[/p][/*][*][p]Steam avatars for players now properly load.[/p][/*][*][p]Scroll messages will no longer get stuck on your screen longer than intended.[/p][/*][*][p]Large refactor of the networking code to enhance stability.[/p][/*][*][p]Many more minor changes too numerous and, frankly, too hard to keep track of to post here![/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: April Progress Report
notes.content:
Hey everyone! I apologize for the radio silence for the past few months. The truth is, after releasing our last update, it became clear to us that some restructuring of the game's code was in order. Bringing you PVP required some very strenuous bug testing. This was in part due to the complicated nature of providing networking for PVP, but it was also largely in part due to the way we were doing things. It became clear to us that, in order to keep the game flexible to change so that we can make modifications to the game's code, and to keep the game stable so that players do not run into constant frustrating issues, we needed to do some reorganizing.

Will this affect the game? If we did our jobs, hopefully, it will appear as though our next update doesn't really do anything. This is a good thing, because it will mean that, while the experience is the same for you, our ability to modify the game becomes easier, which in turn means we can provide more updates of higher quality than before.

We're pushing ourselves constantly to improve our skills and improve the game, so we really appreciate how patient you've all been. We urge you to keep playing and giving us your feedback. We read all of your comments and posts about the game, so please do not be shy. If you'd prefer to use [url=https://discord.gg/xgdj5jgYTh]Discord[/url] instead of posting in Steam's Discussions we now have a place to post feedback there as well. The choice is yours whether to use one or the other! If you would like to join, [url=https://discord.gg/xgdj5jgYTh]please click here.[/url]

notes.title: PVP Update
notes.content:
Happy 2025 everyone! If you've been keeping up since we initially made the game available on Steam, you'll know how long and hard we've been working to bring PVP to you. We're proud to announce that it's here. As previously stated, it was very important to us to resolve as many issues with networking and PVP logic as possible before it made it into your hands, so we apologize for the long wait since our last update.

[b]With this update, you will be able to create and join lobbies to play against each other in PVP matches! [/b]Each lobby has 2 player slots, one for each player, and no more. Functionality is currently very basic, so if you'd like to chat or have spectators, we recommend using a service such as Discord and screen sharing so people can watch, though we ask you not to stream it publicly on services like Twitch, YouTube, or Kick yet. Once you both ready up, things should proceed just as they did when playing against the AI.

And that's it! As simple as this update appears to be, it really did take a lot of work and diligence to get here. These fundamental systems create the groundwork needed for the rest of the game's development, so reaching this point is a major milestone for us on our journey to 1.0. We really hope you have fun with it and look forward to what's to come.

If you wish, you can jump right in by updating the game on steam, or if you want try to find some matches in the community, head on over to the official Skirmish Discord, accessible via a link we'll be sending to backers via email (if you aren't already in there). We do recommend that you skim the list of known issues detailed below you know what to expect, or circle back to this page if you run into trouble to see if your issue is listed. Also check out the pinned threads on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2823430/discussions/]Discussions board[/url] for advice on what to do if you are stuck and need some help.

Known Issues as of 0.2.00:

[h3]Game Breaks with Consecutive Matches[/h3]
Joining another lobby and starting a new match after completing one in the same session can cause your next one to break. [b]We highly recommend closing the game client and relaunching from Steam when you finish a match.[/b]
[h3]Cannot Redeploy or Declare Skirmishes[/h3]
Sometimes characters will become unresponsive when attempting to declare a skirmish between one of your characters to your opponent's, or redeploying to a new lane. [b]We recommend selecting and unselecting a card in your hand as it appears to reset the input system and allow your characters to respond once again.[/b] If this does not work, your character may be lacking the necessary speed to do so, or you may be attempting to do it during the wrong phase of the game.
[h3]Difficulty with Selecting Characters[/h3]
Colliders are currently very tight on characters, so mousing over certain characters with lanky limbs (we're looking at you, Wisp and Mokoi) can be difficult. You may accidentally click a lane instead of a character, which, if you're attempting to declare a skirmish, will frustratingly result in a redeploy instead. We're aware that it's annoying and we're working on a way to fix it for all characters in the future. Until then, the best way to tell that your cursor is on a character and not a lane is to watch for a change in their outline and a subtle change in size.
[h3]Focused Card Stuck on Screen[/h3]
When focusing a card by right clicking a card in your hand, sometimes it can get stuck in the middle of your screen during certain transitions. You can move the camera around using WASD and zooming by scrolling up and down on the mouse wheel if this happens to see around it as a (bad) workaround. It usually resolves when the number of cards in your hand is changed.
[h3]Unable to Focus Certain Cards[/h3]
Certain cards cannot be focused, such as cards that are queued up on the top left and right corners of the screen when someone has played a card, and the cards in the discard piles.
[h3]Question Mark Avatars[/h3]
Steam avatars often do not load when joining a lobby.
[h3]Message Scroll Stuck on Screen[/h3]
The message scroll that provides helpful hints during gameplay can sometimes get confused and remain on your screen long after it is needed.
[h3]General Issues[/h3]
There will be some smaller and less common issues with game logic. Such examples could be characters being targetable when they shouldn't be (or the reverse), resolve, speed, or health being miscalculated, cards not performing quite right, and more. Most of these will not break a game but might result in you or your opponent getting an unintended advantage.

notes.title: December Progress Report
notes.content:
I hope everyone is enjoying the holidays! We're still working diligently to get the next update with multiplayer out. We know this is the main feature of the game and want to get it in your hands so you can finally play games with friends (and enemies). We'd really hoped it would be done by now but with multiplayer, loose ends are a big problem that can affect your experience horribly and we'd rather catch it and fix it internally than have you all deal with it. We really appreciate your patience on this, but I think it'll be, as The Gaben would say, worth the wait.

As before, stay tuned. [b]When this update is ready, we're dropping it ASAP,[/b] so keep checking your Steam library for announcements like this one and feel free to discuss on the Discussions forum!

notes.title: November Progress Report
notes.content:
Hello everyone! We've been silently working for the past 2 months since our last game update on what we hope will be very exciting for everyone: [b]online multiplayer[/b]! Those of you who have played the current build know that this functionality has been teased with inactive menu buttons that have big ugly crosses drawn over them that woefully do nothing when pressed, but not for long. PVP is, obviously, a main feature and draw of the game, and while we're proud of having been able to offer an AI to play games with, we know that PVP is where the vast majority of players are going to be focused. This is why we've been taking care to ensure that online play is not only functional, but also free of as many bugs as possible. We'd love for your first experience into online play to be a positive one, so we're being extra thorough this time.

[b]The upcoming update will allow players to browse, join, and create their own lobbies as well as engage in online PVP[/b]. It sounds simple, but this system is going to be the backbone of online play and getting it working as smoothly as it is has taken a significant amount of effort and care. This will mark a milestone in development for us and bring us one step closer to 1.0.

We can't give an exact date right now, but [b]keep your eyes peeled for an update and/or announcement for this game in your Steam libraries in the next few weeks[/b]. We hope to have it in your hands by the end of November, but, perfectionists that we are, we want to maintain a certain standard for our updates and would prefer to delay an update than to deliver one that is not fun, full of bugs, or frustrating. Please stay tuned and feel free to discuss and ask questions in the Discussions tab of Steam's Community Hub!

notes.title: Hotfix v0.1.03
notes.content:
Codemonkeys here, bringing you an update to help address some issues people were having due to various display sizes. Here is what to expect:

[list]
[*]Each time you restart the game, the game will now check your monitor's supported resolutions and choose the best one based off of your current desktop resolution. Previously it did not do a good job of this and it only mattered the first time you ran the game.
[*]The settings page of the main menu is now dynamically populated with resolutions appropriate for your monitor and the game. These range between 720p and 4k resolutions in the 16:9 aspect ratio. If your monitor is using an aspect ratio outside of this, the largest 16:9 resolutions applicable for your display should appear here, and you may see black bars at the top and bottom or sides of your screen. This is normal, and the game is designed to work this way.
[*]The fullscreen toggle on the setting page of the main menu now switches between Exclusive Fullscreen and Borderless Fullscreen modes. Windowed mode is not supported for now.
[*]On the off chance that you are using a monitor resolution we did not account for, the game should still attempt to acquire a reasonable resolution but it may result in graphical issues. For the best experience, we recommend attempting to set the resolution of the game and your monitor to a 16:9 resolution between 720p and 4k.
[*]If you run into any issues while adjusting your resolution settings and cannot get the game to display correctly, try restarting the game so it can attempt to reacquire an appropriate resolution for you.
[/list]

We hope this resolves some issues some of you were having! Please continue to report any issues you have to the Steam Discussions page in the Community Hub as we are monitoring discussion posts closely.

notes.title: Graphical Fixes In the Works
notes.content:
Ultrawide chads rejoice. A fix is in the works to unbork the screen resolutions, especially when playing the game in 16:9 on an ultrawide monitor. [i](actual ultrawide resolutions will have to come later)[/i]

This should also fix some of the UI clipping off the screen on some people monitors.

[u]This update should also introduce resolution options in the main menu.[/u]

[b]Skirmish should, after this update, detect your largest resolution monitor and apply the closest possible game screen resolution[/b] so that you can choose your resolution settings in the main menu.

Fix should realistically be available by the end of the week, or earlier.
